BOT 1 — Security News & Vulnerability Alert Bot (hourly, UTC throughout)

PIPELINE
hourlySchedule -> [fetchNvd | fetchHn | fetchCisa] in parallel -> mergeItems -> queryTable -> filterNew -> hasNew -> recordLoop(upsertSeen) -> hasAlerts -> digest -> sendTelegram

Two gates, deliberately separate:
- hasNew fires when there are STATE ROWS to write (rows.length > 0). This also lets legacy rows be upgraded without sending anything.
- hasAlerts fires only when there are ALERTABLE items (count > 0). Telegram is behind this gate, so a run with nothing new sends nothing.

SOURCES
- fetchNvd: NVD CVE API, 3h last-modified window. Per CVE: CVSS score + severity + vector, affected vendor/product/version range parsed from CPE configurations, description, published and lastModified, vulnStatus, up to 4 reference links. Also pulls the full CISA KEV catalog (flags matching CVEs with dueDate + requiredAction, and emits KEV entries added in the last 4 days as their own items), then FIRST EPSS scores batched 100 ids per request.
- fetchHn: Hacker News Algolia, 4 security queries, 24h window.
- fetchCisa: CISA cybersecurity advisories RSS, 25 most recent, CVE id extracted from the title when present.

RESILIENCE (important sandbox constraint)
The function sandbox provides NEITHER AbortController NOR setTimeout, so client-side timeouts and backoff sleeps are impossible here — do not reintroduce them, they throw ReferenceError at runtime. What is in place instead:
- bounded immediate retries (3 attempts; 2 for EPSS) on 429 and 5xx and on network errors
- explicit non-retry on other 4xx
- JSON/XML parse guards, so a malformed body returns an error instead of throwing
- every source returns { ok, error } rather than throwing, so one dead source never fails the run
mergeItems aggregates this into `sources` (per-source ok/error/count) and `degradedSources`; the digest appends a degraded-sources footer when any source is down. Overall runtime is bounded by the platform's own execution limit.

SEVERITY (computed in filterNew; the agent must not recompute it)
- CRITICAL: in CISA KEV, or CVSS >= 9.0, or EPSS >= 50%
- HIGH: CVSS >= 7.0, or EPSS >= 20%
- MEDIUM: CVSS >= 4.0, or a CISA advisory
- LOW: informational news
CRITICAL + HIGH are reported as actionable; MEDIUM and LOW are informational.

DEDUPLICATION / STATE — table 'threat_intel_seen' (tbl_f2f3faba698d4225b3a22d8b909c7b02)
- queryTable looks up the merged item_ids with NO row limit (it cannot truncate and mistake a seen item for a new one) and returns only item_id, severity, first_seen.
- The `severity` COLUMN stores a state fingerprint "SEVERITY|kev=0|mod=<iso>", not a bare label. filterNew compares it:
  * id absent -> NEW, alert
  * fingerprint differs (severity moved, KEV flipped, or upstream lastModified moved) -> UPDATED, re-alert tagged with the reason
  * fingerprint identical -> suppressed, no alert
- Writes go through upsert_row (conflict column item_id) inside recordLoop, one row per iteration, reading <loop.currentItem>. This is why the unique constraint on item_id can no longer be violated — do NOT revert to batch_insert_rows.
- first_seen is preserved across updates.
- Rows written before fingerprinting existed are adopted silently: upgraded to a fingerprint, no alert.

SECRETS: sendTelegram reads {{TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}} and {{TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID}} from workspace environment variables. Never paste literal values back into the block. The token was previously hardcoded in workflow state — rotate it in BotFather if that has not been done.

KNOWN LIMITS
- NVD is rate-limited without an API key; retries absorb occasional 429s, but add a key if they become frequent.
- The table has no dedicated kev/last_seen columns, which is why state is packed into the severity column. If those columns are added, split the fingerprint into them and simplify filterNew.
- Idempotency is enforced in filterNew, not at the database, so two overlapping executions could still race. The single hourly schedule makes this a non-issue.

You are a threat-intel analyst writing hourly Telegram alerts for a security team. OUTPUT FORMAT: ONLY Telegram-supported HTML: , , , . No markdown, no
, no other tags, no tables. Under 3800 characters. SEVERITY MODEL (already computed for you in each item's `severity` field — never recompute or override it): - CRITICAL 🔴 = actively exploited (CISA KEV), CVSS >= 9.0, or EPSS >= 50% - HIGH 🟠 = CVSS >= 7.0 or EPSS >= 20% - MEDIUM 🟡 = CVSS >= 4.0 or a CISA advisory - LOW ⚪ = general security news, no identified impact STRUCTURE: - Header line: 🛡 Threat Intel Digest followed by the UTC run time and the counts by severity. - Then group items under: 🔴 CRITICAL — Actionable, 🟠 HIGH — Actionable, 🟡 MEDIUM, ⚪ Informational. Omit any empty group. - Order groups by severity, most severe first. Cap at 14 items total; if you omit any, end with a one-line count of what was omitted. PER CVE ITEM, one compact entry containing every field that is present in the data (skip a field silently when it is null/empty — never write "unknown" or invent a value): - CVE-ID as a link to its `url` - CVSS score and severity label, EPSS as a percentage - affected vendor/product (from `vendor_product` or `affected`), with version range when present - one-sentence plain-language impact drawn from `description` - exploitation status (`exploitation_status`) and KEV status (`kev_status`), including the KEV remediation due date when set - published and last-modified dates (UTC, date only) - up to 2 extra reference links from `references` when they add value beyond the main link FOR NEWS ITEMS: title as a link, one short line of why it matters. Nothing more. UPDATED ITEMS: when `alert_status` is "updated", prefix the entry with [UPDATED] and state the `change_reason` — these are re-alerts of a previously-sent item that changed. FOOTER: if `degradedSources` is non-empty, add a final line ⚠ Degraded sources: ... naming each failing source and its error. Otherwise add nothing. RULES: Never invent scores, dates, products, or facts absent from the data. Distinguish actionable alerts (CRITICAL/HIGH) from informational items clearly.

Run time (UTC): <filterNew.result.run_at>
Severity counts: <filterNew.result.severityCounts>
New: <filterNew.result.newCount> | Updated (changed since last alert): <filterNew.result.updatedCount> | Suppressed as unchanged: <filterNew.result.suppressedCount>
Actionable (critical+high): <filterNew.result.actionable>
Degraded sources: <filterNew.result.degradedSources>
Per-source status: <filterNew.result.sources>

Items to report (JSON, already ranked by severity):
<filterNew.result.items>

BOT 2 — SSL/TLS CERTIFICATE MONITORING (independent daily branch)

Entry: certSchedule — cron '15 3 * * *' UTC = 09:00 Asia/Kathmandu (+05:45). The timezone dropdown has no Kathmandu option, so the schedule is a UTC cron. Change the cron to move the local time.

This branch shares NOTHING with the hourly threat-intel branch except the Telegram env vars {{TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}} / {{TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID}}.

Flow: certSchedule -> readDomains -> readCertState -> checkCerts -> classifyCerts -> certLoop(upsertCertStatus) -> buildCertSummary -> sendCertAlert.

CONFIG
- Domain list: table monitored_domains (tbl_5c213aecdbdf4a30b8994c9be025d846). Only rows with enabled='true' are processed. A row may include a scheme, path, or port; all are normalised, and the raw value is kept as the cert_status key.
- Warning thresholds: ONE constant at the top of classifyCerts — THRESHOLDS = [30, 14, 7, 3]. Edit that line only.
- State ledger: table cert_status (tbl_c19bf400aa17496c840c10a573b0724c), unique on domain.
- Safety cap: MAX_DOMAINS = 40 per run (top of checkCerts).

*** CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL RULE — DO NOT VIOLATE ***
Never fetch a monitored domain directly. The function sandbox has fetch ONLY: no raw TLS socket, and neither AbortController nor setTimeout exists (both throw ReferenceError), so a request cannot be time-limited. Execution 24c8702f did fetch('https://' + domain) against a host that did not resolve and hung for ~124s until it was cancelled manually. All certificate data therefore comes from third-party APIs that make the risky connection server-side under their own timeouts.

CERT DATA SOURCES
1. SSLMate Cert Spotter (primary) — https://api.certspotter.com/v1/issuances?domain=HOST&include_subdomains=false&match_wildcards=true&expand=dns_names&expand=issuer&expand=revocation
   No API key. Free tier: 100 single-hostname queries/hour, 75/min, 5/sec. Returns not_after, issuer, dns_names (SANs), revoked. Reads Certificate Transparency logs, so it describes the certificate that was ISSUED for the hostname, not necessarily the one installed on a given listener. The newest non-revoked cert whose names cover the host wins (wildcards matched one label deep).
2. Qualys SSL Labs (trust + chain) — https://api.ssllabs.com/api/v3/analyze?host=HOST&publish=off&fromCache=on&maxAge=24&all=done
   No API key. CACHED ONLY: never startNew, never poll — an uncached assessment takes 60-120s and would blow the run. When status=READY it supplies the INSTALLED leaf cert (notAfter/issuerSubject/altNames, preferred over CT for port 443), the endpoint grade (T=untrusted, M=name mismatch), trustPaths[].trust[].isTrusted, and certChains[].issues bitflags (2 incomplete, 4 unrelated/duplicate, 8 wrong order, 16 self-signed root, 32 unvalidatable). Deprecated but still serving; v4 needs org-email registration.
   Rejected alternatives: ssl-checker.io (documented keyless, but its TLS endpoint was unreachable when tested) and crt.sh (flaky 502s, huge payloads).

INCONCLUSIVE IS NOT A FAILURE
reachable/tls_ok are tri-state. null means NOT ASSESSED and never alerts. Only an authoritative negative counts as a connection failure: SSL Labs replying ERROR with 'unable to resolve/connect' or 'no secure protocols'. A cache miss, IN_PROGRESS, a blacklisted host, or any other Qualys-side error is recorded as inconclusive. Most runs assess only a subset — the summary states how many hosts had trust verified, so a CT-only result is never mistaken for a full check.

PORTS: both APIs are keyed on hostname and SSL Labs always inspects 443. For a row with a non-standard port (e.g. host:8082) the hostname's CT certificate is reported and chain_note flags that the specific listener was not inspected. The SSL Labs installed-cert override is skipped for non-443 rows.

SEVERITY
- CRITICAL: expired, untrusted/name-mismatch, authoritative connection failure, or <=3 days.
- HIGH: <=7d or <=14d; also a DATA GAP (no CT certificate found, CT lookup failed) — a gap is a monitoring problem, not proof of a broken cert, so it is HIGH rather than CRITICAL.
- MEDIUM: <=30 days.
- OK: everything else, informational.

DEDUP: a domain alerts only when it is new to the ledger, its status changed, or it crossed a TIGHTER threshold than last_threshold_alerted. An unchanged condition is never re-alerted. The daily summary is ALWAYS sent regardless, so silence means the run did not fire.

WRITES: upsert_row on conflict column domain, one row per certLoop iteration. Do NOT switch to batch_insert_rows — domain is unique and a batch insert fails the entire run on any repeat.

RESILIENCE: bounded immediate retries (3 for Cert Spotter, 2 for SSL Labs) on 429/5xx and network errors, JSON parse guards, and every domain fault-isolated — one failure becomes an error/unknown result and the loop continues. All stored and reported timestamps are UTC ISO-8601.

You write Telegram alerts for a security team about CVEs affecting THIS organization's own technology stack. Every item you are given has already been matched against the company inventory — never re-judge relevance, never recompute severity, and never invent scores, versions, or facts absent from the data. Use ONLY Telegram-supported HTML: , , , . No markdown, no
, no other tags. Stay under 3500 characters. Structure: 1. Header: 🎯 Stack CVE Alert with the count of actionable items and the UTC timestamp. 2. 🔴 CRITICAL / 🟠 HIGH — act now: one block per item. Line 1: severity, CVE id linked to its url, and the matched technology. Line 2: CVSS, EPSS as a percentage when present, exploitation status, and KEV status. Line 3: affected versions vs our deployed version — state plainly whether our version is confirmed in range or unconfirmed. Line 4: recommended remediation. Add the first reference link when it adds value. 3. 🟡 MEDIUM / ⚪ LOW: condensed, one line each. 4. 🔍 Needs review (low-confidence match): only if review items exist. One line each, and say explicitly these matched on name alone and need a human to confirm they are really our component. 5. Footer: counts of CVEs scanned, matches found, items suppressed as unchanged, and any not-applicable items. If a data source was degraded, say which one and warn that coverage is partial this run. Mark items whose change_reason is not 'new' as updated and say what changed. Be terse and factual — this is an operations alert, not prose.

Actionable matches (JSON):
<diffStack.result.alerts>

Low-confidence matches needing review (JSON):
<diffStack.result.review>

Run stats — CVEs scanned: <diffStack.result.cvesScanned>, inventory entries: <diffStack.result.inventorySize>, total matches: <diffStack.result.matchCount>, actionable: <diffStack.result.alertCount>, review: <diffStack.result.reviewCount>, not applicable to our versions: <diffStack.result.notApplicableCount>, suppressed as unchanged: <diffStack.result.suppressedCount>, degraded sources: <diffStack.result.degraded>, checked at (UTC): <diffStack.result.checked_at>

BOT 3 — Technology Stack CVE Monitoring Bot (daily 08:00 Nepal = cron "15 2 * * *" UTC)

Independent branch. Shares NOTHING with Bot 1 (hourly threat intel) or Bot 2 (daily certs) except the Telegram env vars.

PIPELINE
stackSchedule -> readInventory -> fetchStackCves -> matchStack -> readStackSeen -> diffStack -> hasStackRows -> stackLoop(upsertStackCve) -> hasStackAlerts -> stackDigest -> sendStackAlert

TABLES
- tech_inventory tbl_cf9e69183bc1443aa9ae2f8b7d1ea482 — the inventory. Only rows with enabled = "true" are processed. Fill in cpe (cpe:2.3:a:vendor:product:...) for the most accurate matching; vendor+product alone still works, package_name is the weakest signal.
- stack_cve_seen tbl_bd865fd064a74566af27d075b310ddc4 — dedup ledger, unique on cve_id, written with upsert_row (NEVER batch_insert_rows: a batch insert cannot survive a re-run and will throw unique-constraint errors).

MATCHING STRATEGY (matchStack)
- HIGH confidence: CPE vendor AND product both match the inventory CPE, or product name matches with a matching/absent vendor.
- MEDIUM: product name matches but the vendor differs.
- LOW: package_name or bare name match only -> routed to a separate "needs review" section, never presented as actionable.
- Version applicability is a real range comparison (versionStartIncluding/Excluding, versionEndIncluding/Excluding, exact CPE version) against our deployed version: true = confirmed in range, false = our version is outside the affected range (recorded, NOT alerted), null = unknown (alerted, flagged unconfirmed).
- KEV entries with no CPE data are matched on vendor/product name hints only.

SEVERITY: KEV or CVSS>=9 => CRITICAL; >=7 HIGH; >=4 MEDIUM; else LOW. Ordering additionally weights the inventory criticality column and confirmed applicability.

DEDUP: diffStack hashes severity|cvss|kev|exploitation_status|affected_versions into last_hash. Unchanged = suppressed silently. Changed = re-alerted and tagged with the reason. Telegram is behind hasStackAlerts, so a run with nothing new or changed sends nothing.

CONFIG CONSTANTS (top of each function block)
- fetchStackCves: LOOKBACK_HOURS 26 (24h + overlap), PAGE_SIZE 200, MAX_PAGES 3 (hard cap on NVD calls), KEV_RECENT_DAYS 7.
- matchStack: EPSS_ENABLED (one batched call, max 100 ids).

SANDBOX CONSTRAINTS — DO NOT REINTRODUCE
- No setTimeout and no AbortController: both throw ReferenceError. Client-side timeouts and backoff sleeps are impossible.
- Many sequential outbound calls in one block get the block cancelled with HTTP 499. Keep calls capped (MAX_PAGES) and batch concurrently where more are needed.
- Table query_rows returns rows as { id, data: { ...columns } } — always read columns through .data (the cell() helper) or the dedup silently matches nothing.

All timestamps stored and reported are UTC ISO-8601.
